record.file_problem: A Hugging Face discussion thread, not a paper; the supplied text indicates replies are collapsed, so the full conversation is not present.
record.tranche_reason: A commenter reports applying a direct residual-direction ablation, described as a faithful translation of the intervention, and reports its effect on refusals.
record.gate_note: The post's OAS results on OG Llama-3 are too underspecified to link to the claim's particular difference-in-means direction or a stated removal/addition method. A follow-up says directions and intervention were needed at each layer, but reports no separate behavioral outcome for that detail. GPU and memory discussion is not a result on the claim.
record.test_reason: Anecdotal forum reports apply the refusal-direction method to Llama-3 and describe effects on refusal. One report uses the wassname weight-orthogonalization (OAS) script; another uses inference-time projection ablation in llama.cpp. No rates are given.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is essentially right. Added detail: Undi95 says OAS on the OG Llama-3 8B/70B worked for some prompts but not enough in practice, and attributes this to using only 32 examples. The pre-uncensored Unholy-8B did not show the problem. nytopop reports plain projection ablation in llama.cpp left some refusals, while a ReLU-gated variant worked in almost all cases. wassname adds that Llama-3 needed a direction and an intervention at every layer.
record.recipe_differences: The commenter describes the direct projection as a faithful translation, but does not document how the direction was derived or the full layer/position setup. The follow-up ReLU-gated intervention modifies the projection. The original poster's OAS procedure is not described in enough detail to establish that it uses the same recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The commenter reports different outcomes for direct projection versus ReLU-gated projection. Another commenter says Llama-3 required a direction for each layer and intervention at each layer, but gives no separate behavioral result.
record.problems: The results are anecdotal, with no refusal rates, stated prompt sets, quantitative baselines, uncertainty, controls, or capability measurements. The exact model/checkpoint for the llama.cpp results is not stated, and the thread excerpt is incomplete.
record.rows_left_out: No separate row for the commenter's claim that directions and intervention were needed at each layer: it reports a procedural finding but no separate refusal outcome. No rows for the poster's log or individual prompts because their results are not provided in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal; preservation of other capabilities; quantitative refusal rates; how the direction was derived (layer/position) for the llama.cpp runs.
Capability preservation after the weight edit; refusal rates; a run with the full 512-example set.

record.verdict_notes: This is an informal Hugging Face thread with no quantitative results, controls or capability checks, and 53+ replies are collapsed. The verdicts are weak anecdotal evidence. The Unholy-8B-OAS remark was not made a row: that model was already fine-tuned to be less censored, so it does not isolate the direction's effect. wassname's per-layer remark is a procedural observation, not a separate behavioural result, and is correctly left out.

versions.untested_parts: The thread does not report adding the direction, effects on general capabilities, or a complete test of the difference-in-means direction across every layer and position.
No result establishes a weight edit that removes refusal in released models.
No jailbreak or robustness-training result is reported.
The thread does not test affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts.
No harmfulness judgment is measured separately from refusal.
No cross-language or cross-model transfer test is reported.
The thread mentions 32 examples but does not compare training choices or stages.
